agent_priors_used: Agent prior, not SPIDER evidence: in long-horizon tool-using systems the dominant failure of a research program is silent capability loss through branch divergence and merge overwrites, not lack of ideas. The program's own evidence corroborates the pattern (15 consecutive MEASUREMENT_INVALID in one Intel thread, 80 Physics experiments with zero valid positives, 106 C-MEAS-VALID experiments) but the specific diagnosis that the accepted kernel was orphaned by a merge is repository fact, not prior.

Agent prior: a comparison is uninformative unless the baseline is strong and the instrument has dynamic range. I use this to prefer building/validating the instrument over generating hypotheses, and it is why a pre-arm executed degeneracy screen is mandated in the lanes that carry the central comparison.

Agent prior: a result that is valid in setting but obtained on a fixture whose dynamic range is degenerate is worse than no result, because it consumes a claim status and manufactures false confirmation. Hence I prefer MEASUREMENT_INVALID with a named smallest next action over any PASS produced by an instrument that cannot discriminate.

Agent prior: strongest baselines are usually reconstructions rather than the headline competitor's own artifact, because headline artifacts depend on unavailable infrastructure. This drives the Intel allocation toward a pinned runnable reference arm over attempting to run a paper's system.

Agent prior: in agent memory research, a registry that constrains exploration can be net-negative on novel tasks (exploration/exploitation asymmetry), so a program must test inherited-mechanism harm, not only inherited-mechanism benefit. I record this as the largest question that remains unasked this cycle because it presupposes an executable inherited arm.

Agent prior: program-level diversity has diminishing returns when several lanes are converging on one underidentified comparison; the correct response is to make the comparison identified, not to add lanes to it. This is why four of six allocations serve one decision, and I state the opportunity cost explicitly rather than hiding it.

allocation.comparative_reasoning: Against C-PARAM-INHERIT: that is Product's live thread and the two would collide on the same kernel recovery. Against C-FRESHNESS or C-DELTA-REPAIR: both already hold valid synthetic SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST results and are blocked on exactly the substrate Runtime is building this cycle, so running them now would be a third consecutive MEASUREMENT_INVALID on transfer. Against C-LLM-INHERIT: no LLM key exists on this runner, so it is unmeasurable rather than merely unfinished. Against a fresh test of whether inherited mechanisms create new failure modes (stale fragment forcing a wrong path, mis-binding cascading): that is a genuinely neglected and valuable question, and I judge it second-order — it presupposes an executable inherited arm and is far better asked next cycle once resolution and parameterization both execute. That is the opportunity cost I am explicitly accepting.
dependencies: Runtime's multi-verb stdlib substrate with per-task state hash (this cycle, parallel; the handoff already specifies a stdlib-only locally served application so it can proceed independently)
NOT dependent on Product's kernel recovery, by design
allocation.question: On a stdlib-only, locally served, multi-endpoint, multi-verb HTTP application in which every registered mechanism's parameter slots are actually bound so that every action template executes, can a fitted applicability gate over bound parameter slots resolve natural-language goals to applicable mechanisms without internal ids, above lexical-overlap and random nulls, while holding pooled false-accept at most 0.10, UNKNOWN precision at least 0.85, and global and per-class ECE at most 0.15 with bootstrap upper at most 0.18 when the calibration quantity is actually fitted rather than fixed by construction — so that abstention is measured instead of algebraically determined? The packet must additionally: define the primary metric as mechanism-identity binding correctness with HTTP postcondition execution demoted to a separate, separately thresholded verification measure, closing the construct-validity defect that made the previous packet's outcome a deterministic function of which mechanism was selected; execute and log a degeneracy screen before any candidate arm runs confirming the lexical-overlap null sits strictly below a preregistered headroom threshold and the comparison leg is non-empty; run a real oracle arm holding mechanism_id with a declared difficulty ceiling; implement per-task server state reset with a logged state hash; hash the candidate resolver, goal generator and server code into freeze.json; and declare explicitly which regime is being measured, so the kernel-level aliasing ceiling and natural-language goal-to-mechanism binding over a real multi-endpoint application stop being read as compatible. The resolver must be evaluated independently of parameterized induction so that its result does not depend on the kernel-recovery thread.
allocation.rationale: Graph is IDLE, C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE is the most neglected load-bearing claim in the registry, and both lanes now running the central comparison presuppose it. Resolution is also the one step a no-memory executor has no answer for at all, so it is where the architectural question actually lives: if goals cannot be resolved to applicable mechanisms with calibrated abstention, inheritance is unaddressable however cheap it is. The claim's last failure was purely construct validity — the metric was derived from HTTP status and was a deterministic function of mechanism selection — which is cheap to fix and does not require new infrastructure. It is the only substantial claim that is HYPOTHESIS, unblocked on this runner, and owned by no other currently active lane.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: The central premise — that a later agent measurably avoids work by inheriting mechanisms rather than by re-searching or by compiling deterministically from the current observation — has never been validly tested in 394 canonical experiments. The snapshot shows why, and the reason is mechanical rather than scientific. I verified in the repository that the inherited arm is structurally non-executable from the canonical tree: src/spider/kernel.py at main HEAD 0602eb6d is 132 lines and contains no distill_parameterized, no align_parameters and no parameterized induction at all; its literal distill() hardcodes confidence=0.5 against min_confidence=0.8, so EXECUTABLE is unreachable (exactly the negative capability fact Frontier measured as 0 of 1200 EXECUTABLE resolutions, and the fact Graph recorded as 'no durable kernel distill_parameterized capability'). Meanwhile the one durable, audit-PASS, unit-tested inheritance capability SPIDER ever produced — commit 664bc124, kernel sha256 ac1cbdd9…, 776 lines, 20/20 tests, verdict ACCEPT_MECHANISM_IN_SETTING with audit producer_claim_supported=true — survives only as an unreachable commit object. I confirmed that no branch tip in the repository contains distill_parameterized. It was orphaned at 3811cfd6, the 'Merge origin/main into lab2/product' commit, which silently reverted the kernel 776 -> 132 lines; the 618-line variant built afterwards (c7b818eb) was itself reverted at a846387b. So the second failure mode is substrate, not code: the second time the inherited arm WAS executable (EXP-PRODUCT-36249064252, 150/150 never-observed-B transfers, binding accuracy 1.0, all three baselines at 0.0 mechanism success) the independent audit showed the economic gate had ZERO dynamic range for any system, because cold exploration already achieved 1.0 HTTP request per task on that substrate. The program's central comparison has therefore failed twice for opposite and equally fixable reasons: the treatment was absent, then the instrument had no range. A third cycle of per-lane hypothesis generation will reproduce the same two failures. I am therefore re-pointing the portfolio at identification, not at new claims: restore the accepted capability durably in the only lane authorized to own src/, build and validate an instrument that provably discriminates, reconstruct the missing strong baselines as runnable pinned references rather than as literature summaries, and then run the one comparison that can actually decide the premise. Two measurement-readiness facts bound everything: this runner has no Playwright install and no ms-playwright cache, so no browser/CDP capture is possible (the frozen Runtime preflight targets a chromium-1243 path that does not exist here); and OPENAI_API_KEY is ABSENT, so C-LLM-INHERIT and any 'real agent' variant of C-PRODUCT-ECON are not measurable in this cycle regardless of design. C-FRESHNESS and C-DELTA-REPAIR are explicitly PARKED with dependency on Runtime's substrate, not forgotten: both already hold valid SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST results on synthetic single-resource substrates and are the first claims to reactivate once a substrate with real session/auth/drift exists. C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY's 9-experiment Frontier streak is a flag, not a verdict; I continued it because the epistemic decomposition it proposes is the only question that can explain an unidentified comparison, and because the frozen Frontier transaction is already that test and must complete under its frozen design.
director_mandate.scout_assessment: The Scout brief was materially useful and I adopted its central diagnosis: the inherited-vs-no-memory leg is unidentified, the incumbent kernel is non-executable, browser provisioning is a hard block, and the epistemic-visibility decomposition is the right discriminating question. I adopted the Frontier decomposition and the Graph C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE reactivation essentially as proposed. I rejected or corrected four points. (1) The Scout treats the kernel problem as a 'distill_parameterized integration failure' to be fixed in Product scope and offers Graph as an alternative owner; that is wrong twice over. Graph's allowed_code_roots are research/harness and research/graph, so Graph cannot fix src/ at all; and the defect is not an unwritten integration but an accepted, audited, committed capability that was lost off-branch. The fix is Product-scoped and is a recovery of a pinned blob, not a rewrite. (2) The Scout's questions_for_director asks whether Intel should obtain and run AgentJIT/COVENANT/TraceCompiler artifacts; those systems are LLM-driven and OPENAI_API_KEY is ABSENT on this runner, so that work is not executable. I redirected Intel to the key-free deterministic baselines instead. (3) The Scout's cross_lane_dependencies frame Runtime's browser provisioning as the single highest-leverage unblocker; on this runner there is no Playwright install and no ms-playwright cache, and the frozen Runtime preflight names a chromium-1243 path that does not exist, so I judged the block to be an environment fact rather than an engineering backlog and redirected Runtime to the substrate that the actual live questions need. (4) The Scout proposes PARKing Physics' predictive-accuracy thread; I went further and made instrument calibration on planted-ground-truth banks a binary gate whose failure retires the paradigm, because an 80-experiment thread with no valid positives and a statistic the audit showed cannot read its own representation should not receive an open-ended ninth repair. The brief's external reconnaissance was used as staff advice only; none of it is treated as SPIDER evidence, and I did no browsing myself.
